motivation: The registered development intervention found different best continuations after the same first incoming hurt cue. Over 256 complete shared states, W-tap scored 90, continued hybrid 194, anti-hybrid 198.5 and the hindsight best of five 240.5. The corresponding outward-edge set contained 139 states, with 40, 77, 80.5 and 97.5 points respectively. Future information provides an upper bound only.
model: Build a single-decision feedforward router over four existing experts: the frozen population MLP, v1 hybrid, anti-hybrid recurrent policy and anti-Hold MLP. All four observe the actual preceding inputs and are primed with the controls the player executed. Open as population. At the first own hurt cue, choose a continuation once, using only current and preceding own-client observations. Never pass an opponent label, clock identifier, future input or outcome into inference. A branch may keep the original policy.
fit: Generate matched return targets for every expert on complete simulator forks at the first actionable hurt cue. Compare W-tap and Hold-W from the same intervention plus full round. Use original sixteen training calendars, both seats, ordinary and adversarial opponents, with declared variations of opening geometry, RTT, timing phase and private opponent draws. Fit a small network to the four ring-out returns. Select regularization, margin required to switch and training step on original eight development clocks; choose before new mirror donors. The privileged best-of-branches score is a ceiling, never a playable entry.
comparison: Evaluate against plain W-tap, Hold-W, all four fixed experts, and a fighter choosing a single fixed expert randomly per fight. Keep opening state, opponent stream, profile, reach, latency and click cap matched. Show average, worst opponent, switch rate and where individual changes help or hurt. Run live on the same bridge and implement deterministic replay of every proposed and applied head. Use the frozen human-derived opponent only as development evidence.
conclusion: If the legal selector cannot beat the fixed population, retain the fixed policy and diagnose the observability of the optimal switch. Do not train on prospective panels.
